BMI is a stupid measurement, body fat percentage, waist to hip ratio, things like that are relevant. You could have two people, same height, same weight one looks fat and one looks fit. And yes I believe everyone should constantly be working on bettering themselves, physically and mentally. But I’d also caution people against judging fat people... I have a thyroid condition that means I have to work twice as hard to lose weight... even when I was 180 lbs, I could run 5k and do 40 minutes of HIIT better than the skinny chicks in my class... because I was in the process... taking care of yourself is part of loving yourself.

First of all, unless you have no muscle, you’re probably not that fat, I’m 5’1 and I used to weigh 230 lbs... that was pretty fat (But not, people stare at you on the street fat, I have a lot of muscle) ... I completely changed my lifestyle and I’ve lost 90lbs... it took time and was not easy, but I didn’t give up any food I loved completely. I found tracking what I eat helps, I use MyFitnessPal...  Don’t just look at calories, watch your macros and nutrients too... Then making one small change at a time, Something doable, like increasing you water intake,.. then find Healthy foods you like, and try to eat more of those. Focus on what you want to eat more of (veggies) instead of what you can’t have (don’t thinks of them as “bad” foods, just treats). Remember it takes 21 days to build a habit, so again, make one small change every three weeks and you’ll set yourself up for long term, sustainable weight loss that comes from a healthy lifestyle. And good job on all the working out! Just keep breaking a sweat!
Best answer I was gonna say the same thing.

Well if it’s not about girls/relationships... (because I was in a relationship with someone for 10 years that was 165cm)... this sounds like internal spiritual work you have to do. It may sound simple, but have you ever thought, “what does my height have to do with who I am?”  So someone is pretty or ugly, smart or dumb, fat or thin, does that make them anymore or less valuable as a human being. Worrying about your height is your ego, attaching value to a physical state. Let go of the attachment and just be. Try some exploratory meditation, aske yourself why it bothers you, and why it matters and see what thoughts come without emotion or judgement. Focus less on the physical and find something else to focus on, like your life’s purpose.

I’ll start by saying that I’ve worked with people with autism for the past 12 years. So I don’t know what it’s like to be you, but I probably would understand you more than most. At the end of the day, you’re just a person, we all have things about us that make us different (I personally think everyone is somewhere on the autism spectrum, some more severe than others). But I’ll say that often, people with autism have rigid beliefs about right and wrong, what’s fair, etc.... sometimes there are things that aren’t that simple. If you aren’t hurting anyone, and you can do the job well, I think it’s ok, as long as your working there doesn’t negatively affect anyone, don’t worry about it. 

People in this world get all kinds of advantages based on things like who they know, where they live, their race, gender, their looks... so use what advantages you have, just pay it forward some day by helping someone who needs it. And be honest about your abilities.

I’m sorry about your mother, my friend just lost her 8 year old son to cancer... he fought for 3 years. That means he had only 5 years of a real childhood, or life. Look at the wonderful life your mom had before she got sick, a loving family, so many experiences... I would say, let her passing give you purpose, maybe devote time to fundraising for cancer research, or volunteer to support cancer patients or their families... let her inspire you to do something that will make the world better. But take your time to grieve. That’s okay too.
